subject: Acme trial follow-up: procurement readiness & commercial path
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Jenna Morris <jenna.morris@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme trial follow-up: procurement readiness & commercial path

Hi Sam / Jenna —

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clear context on the pilot goals and success criteria. Quick recap and next steps to keep momentum toward a trial->paid conversion: 

1) Trial success criteria (what we heard)
- 3 teams (Search, Recommendations, Support Automation) run representative traffic flows
- 75% latency under 250ms P95 for ensemble queries
- Quality check: parity vs current baseline on the recommendations rerank metric (MRR)
- 2-week opinionated evaluation window starting when you enable billing

2) Commercial path & procurement readiness
- You indicated procurement prefers Purchase Order for anything > $50k/year.
- Marketplace option (AWS Marketplace) is interesting to you for simpler billing — you asked whether we can bill through Marketplace and still get committed capacity. Short answer: yes, we can support Marketplace listing + reserved capacity with an enterprise order.
- We discussed card payment for initial POC spend (< $5k) to speed work while procurement aligns.

3) Paper process items we can prepare
- Draft SOW + trial terms
- Redwood standard SLA + draft DPA
- PO template (attached) — happy to pre-fill if you send the billing contact

4) Next steps
- Sam: confirm preferred billing path (PO vs Marketplace) by end of week (4/23).
- Jenna: share procurement billing contact and PO template fields we should pre-fill.
- Redwood (Marissa): share draft SLA and PO template + demo follow-up with Michael (Solutions Eng) to validate test traffic profiles.

Attachments: redwood-sla-Draft.pdf (draft SLA), po-template-Acme.docx

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if that accelerates things.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (510) 555-0142

---
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenna Morris <jenna.morris@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme trial follow-up: procurement readiness & commercial path

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. Quick answers from procurement side: 

- We prefer PO for any commitment; for a short initial pilot (under $5k) we can do a card to get started.
- Marketplace would be ideal for our finance team as it simplifies invoicing, but we need to confirm whether a committed-reserved SKU is supported there. If Redwood can provide an offer via AWS Marketplace that maps to a reserved capacity SKU, procurement will lean that way.
- I'll introduce our Procurement contact (procurement@acme.com) on this thread and share the specific PO fields we require (billing address, tax id, approver contact).

One clarification: when you say "start of billing" — do you mean start billing immediately at trial activation or only once the teams hit the agreed usage thresholds? We prefer not to start committed billing until baseline usage is validated in your environment.

Sam
Director, Engineering — Acme Corp
sam.patel@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Jenna Morris <jenna.morris@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme trial follow-up: procurement readiness & commercial path

Hi Sam — thanks, and welcome Procurement team. 

Short answers: 
- Billing start: we can support a two-stage approach. Redwood can enable a trial environment and bill only for card-based POC usage initially. If you choose reserved/committed capacity (PO or Marketplace subscription), we can set a billing start date tied to either (A) your acceptance of the SOW or (B) when the agreed usage thresholds are met (i.e., teams enabled and X tokens / API calls reached). We're flexible — happy to be explicit in the trial terms.

- Marketplace + Reserved Capacity: Redwood supports AWS Marketplace Private Offers for committed capacity. I'll loop Michael to confirm the SKU mapping and procurement flow.

I've attached the draft SLA and a PO template to speed procurement. For the PO path we typically require: billing contact, billing address, PO number, and expected start date. If you want Redwood to pre-fill the PO template, please send the billing contact details.

Next step: Michael (cc'd) — can you confirm the Marketplace SKU mapping and whether we can configure a start-date gating in the billing workflow? Also can you propose a short test-traffic profile (sample qps and payload sizes) so Acme can validate latency SLOs during the 2-week evaluation window?

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sla-Draft.pdf, po-template-Acme.docx
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>, Jenna Morris <jenna.morris@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme trial follow-up: procurement readiness & commercial path

Hi all — looping in Rachel from Commercial Ops to help with PO/Marketplace specifics. Quick answers and action items from the Solutions/Prod side: 

1) Marketplace SKU mapping: we have a reserved-capacity SKU that can be offered as a Private Offer on AWS Marketplace. The SKU maps to a commitment tier (e.g., 2x, 4x, 8x GPUs) and has a start date field we can set in the Marketplace offer. That allows you to accept the offer and set an activation/start date later.

2) Billing gating options: we can implement billing start tied to SOW signature or to a usage threshold. If you choose usage gating, we recommend a soft threshold (example: 100k tokens across the three teams OR 10,000 ensemble queries) to avoid false positives; Michael can adjust based on your traffic profile.

3) Test traffic profile (suggested) for validating latency SLO:
- Phase 1 (warm-up): 5 QPS sustained for 1 hour
- Phase 2 (validation): 15 QPS sustained for 4 hours, 95th percentile latency target < 250ms
- Payloads: mix of small (<=512 tokens) and medium (<=2k tokens) requests reflecting your Search and Reranker flows

Rachel will follow up with the pre-filled PO and an internal checklist for Marketplace Private Offer steps.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min call to finalize.

—Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
